column2: Build and maintain shelters for critical climate hazards
column3: "Build and maintain shelters for critical climate hazards" involves building and maintaining shelters in high-risk areas to protect residents during extreme weather events such as floods, cyclones, storms, landslides, extreme heat events or other critical climate hazards. Shelters should meet resilient design standards, including wind- and flood-resistant construction, and be strategically located to maximize accessibility for vulnerable populations. Where possible, shelters can serve multipurpose roles as schools or community centers. Clear funding mechanisms and defined responsibilities for operations and maintenance are essential to ensure long-term reliability and effectiveness.

column2: Implement urban cooling and shading measures in streets, public spaces and buildings
column3: Implement measures to reduce heat absorption and mitigate the urban heat island effect in streets, public spaces and buildings, including reflective coatings, light-colored materials, permeable surfaces, cool pavements, cool roofs, green roofs and walls, shade structures such as shade sails and canopies, and drought-tolerant trees. Municipal governments can pilot these approaches in the most heat-exposed areas, integrate them into routine street upgrades, public-space improvements and public building retrofits, and assess cost–benefit outcomes to guide broader implementation. These measures improve indoor and outdoor thermal comfort, reduce heat stress and energy demand for cooling, manage stormwater, enhance urban livability and biodiversity, and strengthen resilience to rising temperatures.

column2: Build safe housing and implement urban rehabilitation, relocation and resettlement for populations living in high-risk areas
column3: The priority of this action is to build safe housing and implement urban rehabilitation, relocation and resettlement for populations living in areas prone to landslides and flooding, as the housing deficit is one of the main factors related to these threats. This will be implemented through the construction of new housing units in safe locations for family resettlement, the transfer of households exposed to climate hazards to safer locations, and infrastructure upgrades such as slope stabilization and improved drainage systems within vulnerable communities. Relocation and resettlement should include eligibility criteria, participation mechanisms, compensation arrangements, and the identification of safe destination areas with sanitation, lighting, transport, and other essential services. Residents should participate in the design, prioritization, and monitoring of rehabilitation, relocation and resettlement measures in favelas and vulnerable communities.

These actions support early intervention, prevent landslides and erosion, and reduce geohydrological disaster risks.

column2: Strengthen coastal protection infrastructure
column3: Strengthen coastal protection infrastructure strategies include the construction of sea walls and protective structures to mitigate the impact of rising sea levels and coastal erosion. This adaptation measure enhances the resilience of coastal areas and protects communities from the impacts of climate change. Crucially, these interventions must be developed through an integrated coastal management framework, prioritizing nature-based solutions where feasible, to avoid negative downstream effects and ensure equitable protection for all vulnerable communities. Examples include beach nourishment and slope protection measures in urbanized coastal areas and coastal communities.

column2: Develop and implement an integrated climate action plan and risk reduction plan

Review the plan periodically to reflect updated climate scenarios and territorial diversity.

column2: Develop and implement an extreme weather preparedness and emergency response plan
column3: Develop and implement a municipal preparedness and emergency response plan for climate-related extreme events to enable rapid, coordinated action and minimize impacts on the population. The plan should define climate risk scenarios, activation thresholds, roles and responsibilities, command and interdepartmental coordination arrangements, communication and public alert protocols, evacuation routes, emergency shelters, and procedures for reaching vulnerable populations. It should also establish contingency arrangements for essential services, emergency food and water supply, health care, sanitation, electricity, telecommunications, transport and logistics, including supplier mapping, emergency procurement procedures, contingency stocks, distribution points and alternative routes. Measures should include training, simulation exercises, resource and equipment inventories, agreements with local and regional partners, procedures for damage and needs assessment, and protocols for response, recovery and regular plan review after events and exercises. Where relevant, include trained and equipped rural first-response capacity for forest and agricultural fire prevention and response, as well as contingency measures for arboviruses when climate conditions increase transmission risks.

column2: Secure land tenure, essential services and climate-resilient livelihoods for vulnerable rural and traditional communities
column3: Secure land tenure and strengthen climate-resilient livelihoods for vulnerable rural and traditional communities through integrated territorial support. Measures include land regularization and equitable access to land; climate-resilient basic and productive infrastructure in rural settlements; community-based water management and water storage for irrigation and livestock; decentralized renewable energy for households and productive uses; access to adapted machinery, implements and clearly defined social technologies; and technical, extension and financial assistance. Implementation should prioritize women, youth, Indigenous peoples, quilombola communities and other traditional peoples and communities facing persistent social, climate and land-tenure vulnerability. Support should connect secure tenure and essential services to agroecological practices, soil management, resilient production, processing, storage and market access, while ensuring that each intervention has a clear adaptation pathway and avoids duplicating broader public-infrastructure, health or urban-development actions.

column3: Strengthen access to selective waste collection through locally appropriate arrangements that respect applicable legal, institutional, and territorial conditions. Measures may include voluntary drop-off points, support for waste picker cooperatives, adaptable collection schedules, infrastructure improvements, and public awareness. Better waste management reduces pollution, pest and disease-vector proliferation, and associated risks of disease transmission, particularly for vulnerable populations.
